question: What is the main problem in heart failure?

options.A: Inability of the heart to pump blood effectively
options.B: Sudden electrical arrest of the sinoatrial node
options.C: Complete closure of the main coronary arteries
options.D: Hypertrophy of the right atrium without fluid retention

explanation: Heart failure happens when the heart muscle cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the main goal of giving medicines for heart failure?

options.A: eliminate the need for dietary sodium restriction entirely
options.B: permanently cure underlying structural heart valve defects
options.C: increase systemic blood pressure to maximum normal limits
options.D: interrupt harmful neurohormonal pathways and reduce workload

explanation: Drug therapy targets the body's stress hormones to slow down heart damage and make the heart's job easier. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do patients often switch from ACE inhibitors to ARBs?
explanation: A buildup of a chemical called bradykinin from ACE inhibitors often causes an annoying dry cough, leading doctors to switch patients to ARBs. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why are ACE inhibitors and ARBs helpful for a weak heart?

options.A: They decrease afterload and stop harmful cardiac remodeling
options.B: They stimulate rapid heart rate to clear fluid buildup
options.C: They directly dissolve blood clots inside the coronary veins
options.D: They replace lost electrolytes directly in the kidney tubules

explanation: Blocking these body pathways lowers the pressure the heart has to fight against and prevents unhealthy changes in heart shape. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h2)

question: How should beta-blocker treatment usually be started in heart failure?

options.A: Only after surgical valve replacement is completed
options.B: At maximum strength doses immediately on admission
options.C: As a single intravenous bolus during acute distress
options.D: At very low doses with slow upward titration

explanation: Starting with a tiny dose and increasing it slowly prevents the heart from getting overwhelmed at first. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h3)

question: What should a nurse watch for closely when a patient starts taking carvedilol?

options.A: sudden spikes in daytime body temperature
options.C: extreme narrowing of the visual field
options.D: hyperactivity and inability to sleep at night

explanation: Beta-blockers slow the heart rate and can cause temporary fluid buildup before the patient starts feeling better. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h3)

question: How do loop diuretics like furosemide work in the body?

options.A: constricting afferent renal arterioles to reduce glomerular filtration
options.B: blocking sodium and chloride reabsorption in the loop of Henle
options.C: increasing potassium retention inside the distal convoluted tubule
options.D: stimulating aldosterone production directly in the adrenal cortex

explanation: Loop diuretics stop the kidneys from reabsorbing salt and water in a specific part called the loop of Henle, causing heavy urination to clear fluid. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h4)

question: A patient on strong furosemide therapy complains of muscle cramps and weakness. Which electrolyte level is likely low?
explanation: Furosemide flushes out potassium along with extra water, leading to low potassium levels that cause cramps and weakness. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is a classic sign of digoxin toxicity?

options.D: bright red spots floating in the air

explanation: Seeing yellow-green halos around lights is a well-known warning sign that there is too much digoxin in the body. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why does low blood potassium make digoxin more dangerous?

options.A: Low potassium stops the liver from metabolizing the drug molecules
options.B: Hypokalemia directly stimulates the sinoatrial node to beat faster
options.C: Potassium deficiency causes the kidneys to retain all circulating digoxin
options.D: Potassium and digoxin compete for the same binding sites on cell pumps

explanation: Potassium and digoxin fight for the same spots on heart cell pumps. When potassium is low, digoxin takes over those spots more easily and causes toxicity. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why are intravenous vasodilators used in acute heart failure?

options.A: stimulate the sinoatrial node to produce tachycardia
options.B: increase total blood volume through fluid expansion
options.C: rapidly reduce cardiac preload and afterload
options.D: permanently cure underlying coronary artery blockages

explanation: IV vasodilators quickly open up blood vessels, taking the heavy pressure off a struggling heart during an emergency. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is close monitoring necessary when giving strong inotropic drugs through an IV?

options.A: they carry a high risk of dangerous hypotension and arrhythmias
options.B: they completely stop kidney function within the first hour
options.C: the drugs crystallize instantly if the tubing gets too cold
options.D: patients always develop severe skin rashes at the IV site

explanation: These drugs strongly affect heart rhythm and blood pressure, so nurses must watch the patient constantly to prevent dangerous drops or irregular beats. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which home habit is most important for catching worsening heart failure early?
explanation: Stepping on the scale every day is the easiest and fastest way to spot hidden fluid buildup before symptoms get severe. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is a major challenge to taking heart medications consistently in many Nigerian hospitals and homes?

options.A: patients refusing to swallow any form of oral tablet
options.B: high out-of-pocket costs and substandard drug products
options.C: an absolute lack of any government-approved hospitals
options.D: the requirement for daily intravenous injections at home

explanation: Patients often struggle to buy their drugs due to high expenses, and fake or poor-quality drugs can make treatment unreliable. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T1#GNS223_U1_T1_h7)
